whatFailed: GET /api/articles/<documentId> returned 200 with the document object under `data` carrying no `meta` key, although the REST API reference lists `meta` (object) among the keys of the single document object itself.

docClaim.quote:
Requests return a response as an object which usually includes the following keys:

- `data`: the response data itself, which could be:
  - a single document, as an object with the following keys:
    - `id` (integer)
    - `documentId` (string), which is the unique identifier to use when querying a given document,
    - the attributes (each attribute's type depends on the attribute, see [models attributes](/cms/backend-customization/models#model-attributes) documentation for details)
    - `meta` (object)
  - a list of documents, as an array of objects
  - a custom response

- `meta` (object): information about pagination, publication state, available locales, etc.

observed: 200 with body {"data":{"id":2,"documentId":"oxu7drtrrz6081a4c0mcn43n","title":"Guard Published Article",...,"locale":"en"},"meta":{}}. `meta` exists exactly once, as a sibling of `data` at the top level, and is an empty object; the document object under `data` has only id, documentId and the flattened attributes. server.stderr.txt is empty, no error path involved.
impact: Low but real developer friction: anyone typing the documented shape (or generating a client/type from it) will declare a per-document `meta` object that the REST API never emits, on any Strapi 5 content type, in either response format. No data loss, no security impact.

rootCause.file: strapi/documentation: docusaurus/docs/cms/api/rest.md (the doc bug). Product side that fixes the true shape: packages/core/core/src/core-api/controller/transform.ts in the tested worktree.
rootCause.explanation: The `meta` bullet is indented one level too deep in the docs list, so it reads as a key of the single document object rather than as the sibling of `data` that the very next bullet already declares (`- \`meta\` (object): information about pagination, publication state, available locales, etc.`). The product is right and the page's own examples agree with the product: every JSON sample on the same page (lines 157, 210, 301, 382 of the snapshot) shows `meta` beside `data`, never inside the document. In code, `transformResponse` (transform.ts:39-71) is the single place that shapes every core content API response and it returns exactly `{ data, meta }`, with `meta` defaulting to `{}`; `collection-type.ts` findOne calls `this.transformResponse(sanitizedEntity)` with no meta argument, which is why the observed top-level `meta` is `{}`. The document object itself is either the sanitized entity passed through untouched (Strapi 5 flattened default) or, under the deprecated `strapi-response-format: v4` header, `transformEntry`'s `{ id, documentId, attributes }` (transform.ts:146-150). Neither branch has ever attached a `meta` key to an entry, so no configuration of the tested build can satisfy the bullet as written. The bullet is a Strapi v4 carryover: in the v4 code the entry type declared an optional `meta?: Record<string, unknown>` and the return literally carried `// NOTE: not necessary for now  // meta: {}` commented out (see git show a4814d75e4:packages/core/core/src/core-api/controller/transform.ts), so the documented key was aspirational even in v4.

introducedBy.pr: none (direct commit on strapi/documentation, subject "Add REST API documentation"; the GitHub commit-to-PR lookup returns nothing and the ancestry path to main has no merge commit)
introducedBy.title: Add REST API documentation
introducedBy.note: git blame on strapi/documentation main (HEAD c768c7bf5, 2026-08-15) pins the `- `meta` (object)` line and the sibling `meta` bullet to this v4-era commit by Pierre Wizla. The surrounding lines were rewritten twice since (9358b6c86 2024-03-19 "Rename entries to documents in REST API", eba970e24 2025-02-06 "Move files and fix broken links") and both rewrites carried the misplaced bullet through untouched. On the product side the vestigial per-entry meta was deleted by commit a6af41a645 (2024-03-04, PR #19675 "chore: content-api response format header", merged 2024-03-05), the Strapi 5 flattening change that dropped `meta?` from `TransformedEntry` and made the default response the raw flattened document. So: old doc text, newer code, and the two have disagreed since 2024.

issues.title: [Bug]: No meta object in GET response
issues.note: Same family of confusion (a user expected a `meta` object that the response did not carry), but it is about the top-level pagination meta on a v4 GET, not about the misplaced per-document bullet. Closed as completed 2022-07-04.

fixedAfter.note: Docs: strapi/documentation main at HEAD c768c7bf5 (2026-08-15) still has the bullet nested under the single document object (docusaurus/docs/cms/api/rest.md:118); last touch to that file is 3095d316 (2026-07-21, PR #3341, endpoint component redesign) and it did not move the bullet; no open PR addresses it. Product: `git log c43e9ee1e2..origin/develop -- packages/core/core/src/core-api/controller/` is empty, so develop still shapes responses as `{ data, meta }` and the failure would reproduce identically on today's develop.

colleagueFinding.note: Does not map to any of the researcher's 8 Strapi findings; those are all MCP server or admin token items. It is however the same class as their finding 8 (docs materially wrong), and adds a third doc drift, this one in the core REST reference rather than in MCP or admin token text. Their blame work is untouched by this one.

notes: The fix is a one-character-class edit: de-indent `- `meta` (object)` in docusaurus/docs/cms/api/rest.md from four spaces to the top level, or simply delete it, since the top-level `meta` bullet two lines below already documents it correctly. The scenario was authored deliberately red for exactly this drift (see its `note:` in the yaml), and the evidence confirms the reading is fair: the sentence, taken as written, promises a key the product has never emitted. Worth telling the doc author that the same list also survived the v4 to v5 rewrite unaudited, so a sweep of the Requests section against a live Strapi 5 response is warranted. Only one assertion in the scenario failed; the sibling assertion `data exists` passed, and the response is otherwise exactly what the page's own examples show.
